content.text:
Yes — and most of the hard groundwork already exists.

Right now JSHack has:

- 82 authored spells in [spells.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/rules/data/spells.js)
- Per-spell visual events and FX
- A sound registry and audio buses in [sounds.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/display/audio/sounds.js)
- Audio wiring for many spell events in [audioWiring.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/display/audio/audioWiring.js)
- An action recorder, but it records gameplay/proof actions—not video, visuals, or audio

What it does not currently have is a “spell showcase” or video recorder.

The best version would be:

1. Open a special deterministic showcase arena.
2. Automatically cast every spell against prepared targets.
3. Show the spell name and a clean camera framing.
4. Wait for each effect and sound to finish.
5. Record the canvas plus game audio into a video.

Difficulty:

- Automated spell showcase: medium, probably a few focused implementation sessions.
- Audio coverage for every spell: medium; many already work, but some spells share sounds or have no dedicated sound.
- One-click downloadable video: harder, because browser `MediaRecorder` needs both canvas capture and audio routed into a recording stream.
- External OBS/browser recording: easy and could work almost immediately once the showcase mode exists.

I’d build it in two stages: first a polished “spell gallery” that plays every spell in-game, then optional recording/export. That gives us something useful even before tackling video encoding and audio capture.
Even if was a special arg, actually, a special arg would work legitimately, right?!

Yes—absolutely. A special argument is a legitimate, clean solution.

For example:

```text
/index.html?mode=spell-reel
```

That mode could:

- Create a controlled showcase arena
- Spawn safe targets
- Cast every spell through the normal canonical spell pipeline
- Display the spell name
- Play its real in-game visuals and audio
- Optionally record the canvas/audio output

It would be isolated from normal gameplay, so it wouldn’t affect saves, balance, or ordinary runs. For automated/headless use, we could also support something like:

```bash
deno task spell-reel --all
```

So yes: a special showcase argument is probably the cleanest way to build this.
then I could just record on my phone

Exactly. A special spell-reel mode would let you open the game, start the showcase, and record the screen and sound directly with your phone.

That avoids the harder built-in video-export work. We’d only need to make the showcase:

- deterministic and cleanly framed
- slow enough for each effect to read
- labeled with the spell name
- quiet between spells
- able to cycle through all spells or selected categories

That’s substantially easier and would still produce a genuine in-game “super edit.”

cool -- make it so that would be awesome

I was leaning towards the HTML (without regressing the game of course)

I’ll add this as an opt-in HTML/query-parameter showcase mode, leaving the normal game path untouched. First I’m checking the current worktree and the page bootstrap so the feature can hook into existing spell/audio pipelines without creating a parallel casting path.

There is already a `?audio` debug path in the project, which is exactly the right seam to extend. I’m inspecting that mode now; if it already builds a clean arena and grants spells, I can turn it into the phone-recordable reel with minimal risk instead of inventing a second debug system.

The existing `?audio` mode already builds a safe, isolated stage and grants a spell set. I’m going to add a separate `?spellreel` opt-in on top of that: it will reuse the same stage, queue real `CastSpellIntent`s, advance one game turn at a time, and provide start/pause/next controls with the current spell name on screen. Normal URLs and saves will not enter this path.

The first pass is in place: `?spellreel` now reuses the existing audio arena, adds a phone-friendly overlay, and casts through the normal ECS intent pipeline. I’m checking the edge cases now—especially target selection, stamina/resource field names, and architecture/tests—before I call it usable.

Architecture checks pass. One verification command had a typo—the repository has no `tests/runtimeConfig.test.mjs`; I’m rerunning the real focused audio tests and then I’ll use the project’s runtime proof tooling to catch startup/runtime issues that static checks can’t see.

content.text:
Implemented the opt-in spell reel.

Use:

```text
/index.html?spellreel
```

It will:

- Skip character creation and saved games
- Build the existing isolated audio showcase arena
- Grant the authored spells and abundant resources
- Cast 78 visual/action spells through the normal `CastSpellIntent` pipeline
- Keep the target near the player for phone recording
- Show spell name/progress
- Provide Start, Pause, Resume, and Next controls

I excluded fishing, hearthstone, homecoming, and resurrection because they transition or require special world state rather than making useful showcase footage.

Files changed:

- [spellReel.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main/debug/spellReel.js)
- [runtimeConfig.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main/config/runtimeConfig.js)
- [main.js](/home/pjensen/Repos/JSHack/src/main.js)

Verified with `deno check`, audio tests, architecture guards, headless runtime, and `git diff --check`.
